name: Sentry

evidence.errors: E01: SDK exception events become grouped issues; the core product
evidence.uptime: U01, U02: outside HTTP checks; 1 monitor included, more on paid plans
evidence.logs: L02: structured logs with search, export and trace links
evidence.performance: A01: tracing with spans and profiling; tracing is billed in spans
evidence.cron: J01, J02: cron monitors with check-ins for scheduled jobs

line: Error tracking, plus logs, tracing, uptime and cron monitors.

free.text: Developer plan: 5k errors a month, 1 user, 30-day history

errors.math: Developer plan is $0. It includes 5k errors a month, which exactly covers 5,000 errors. Developer has no pay-as-you-go budget, so extra errors are dropped.
Team is $29 a month when billed monthly ($26 a month billed yearly). It includes 50k errors, which exactly covers 50,000 errors.
Team $29 + 50,000 errors at $0.0003625 + 400,000 errors at $0.0002188 = $134.65 estimate. Docs don't say whether band rates apply to all errors or only inside each band, so this may be high.

uptime.math: Team $29 + 4 extra uptime monitors at $1 each = $33 a month. Pricing page says $1 per uptime alert; docs say $1 per monitor. Developer has one monitor and no pay-as-you-go budget.
Team $29 + 24 extra uptime monitors at $1 each = $53 a month. Same pricing conflict as the 5-endpoint row. The docs price monitors, not check runs.
Team $29 + 99 extra uptime monitors at $1 each = $128 a month. Same pricing conflict. Sentry does not offer the own-domain status page in this scenario.
